It'll now be easier for servicemembers to access mental health treatment when they need it. Our bill, named in honor of Arizona sailor Brandon Caserta, is going to save lives.
https://t.co/SH1sd7X3B5

Arizona is dealing with the real-time effects of drought. I've introduced a bill that will help lessen the impacts of Colorado River drought restrictions, while enabling the Colorado River Indian Tribes full exercise of their water rights.
https://t.co/IQuOWE3VvB

The bill we passed in honor of Brandon Caserta will confront military suicides head-on and save the lives of young servicemembers.

I met this week with Brandon's brave parents and other advocates to talk about improving access to mental health treatment in the armed forces. https://t.co/usarajVNds

As Dr. Karuppana of @ValledelSolAZ said, my plan to lower prescription drug costs will improve the lives of her patients by making the treatment they need more accessible and affordable. https://t.co/qpQBpLN8K8

Thanks to the bipartisan bill we passed last week, more Arizona students can continue receiving free school meals this summer.
https://t.co/mIfXWzfZab

This will help provide Arizona kids with healthy school meals that are essential to their success and wellbeing. I’ll continue working with Republicans and Democrats so that Arizona’s schools have the resources needed to deal with rising food costs.
https://t.co/PHZvvCbC6P

According to @AZDHS, more than five people die every day from an overdose in Arizona. This is Overdose Awareness Week, and I’m working to improve access to treatment for substance use disorder and stop the flow of illegal drugs into our communities to prevent these tragic deaths.

This Breast Cancer Awareness Month, a reminder that the best ways to combat this disease are early detection and accessible treatment. I will keep working to ensure Arizonans have access to affordable preventive care.

The PACT Act is law and veterans exposed to toxins during their service can now receive the treatment they need. The VA is already accepting claims, check to see if you or your family member qualify. For more information, visit: https://t.co/Mg1KbH3ekY https://t.co/nwiLvkH0Mk

Cesar Chavez’s fierce commitment to worker’s rights led to higher wages, safer working conditions, and better treatment of workers. As we continue to fight for a more equitable future, we can all learn from his perseverance in the face of injustice. #CesarChavezDay

A government shutdown would have serious impacts.

Servicemembers won't get their paychecks. 
Airports could have major delays. 
Nutrition assistance for children could be cut off.

We can’t let any of that happen. Congress needs to work together to prevent a shutdown.

One man shared that he had been diagnosed with multiple sclerosis in 2021 and had struggled to work because of his condition. Without Medicaid, the cost for his treatment, including MRIs and infusion treatments, would be way too expensive. https://t.co/A7l9gPcAgl

Defunding programs meant to prevent infant deaths isn’t very pro-life. No one asked for this.
https://t.co/V8uc1f6Md4

I cosponsored this amendment and we're voting on it now.

States shouldn't get special treatment, and especially not for making mistakes. That's everything that's wrong with Washington.

We should have a system that helps hardworking families put food on the table no matter where they live.

While most parents can keep their kids on their insurance until age 26, that’s not true for military families on TRICARE. Servicemembers have earned high-quality, affordable health care for themselves and their families and there’s no reason why their benefits shouldn't be the same as private plans. Our bipartisan Healthcare Fairness for Military Families Act will fix this.

60 years ago today, Medicare and Medicaid were created to provide affordable health care for American seniors and working families. Now they’re under attack, and millions of Americans could soon lose their Medicaid coverage because of Trump’s big bill. In the richest country in the history of the world, no one should go bankrupt getting the care they need.

.@MartinOMalley and I heard from folks directly hurt by Trump’s bill at a town hall in Tucson yesterday. Cuts to Medicaid and threats to Social Security and Medicare put Arizonans and their families at risk. I’m fighting to protect the benefits they’ve earned. https://t.co/QKRqxNMYuT

Next year, premiums are expected to rise by an average of 26% for Arizonans with health insurance through the Affordable Care Act. That’s going to hit families hard.

All because Donald Trump and Congressional Republicans’ passed a law that gave tax breaks to rich people paid for by working Americans. But the fight isn’t over. Congress can still act to stop these hikes and protect your health care.

Happening now: @MayorGallego and I are joining local health care leaders to talk about how huge cuts to Medicaid are going to affect your ability to get affordable care when you need it.

Watch the conversation live here:

Thank you to @MayorGallego and all the community leaders who joined us to talk about Medicaid in Phoenix. With more than 300,000 Arizonans at risk of losing their insurance because of Trump and Republicans’ big bill, it’s critical for us to work together to protect folks’ health care.

It’s been 105 years since America finally gave women the constitutional right to vote, a milestone that launched decades more struggle until women across the country could fully exercise that right. That only happened because of a lot of brave, patriotic Americans. We have to carry on that legacy as we keep fighting to defend the right to vote.

RFK Jr. is lying to the American people. Two months ago to the day, Donald Trump signed his big bill cutting Medicaid by nearly $1 trillion.

Today, our country's leading health official is pretending those cuts don't even exist.

Medicare is testing AI in 6 states, including Arizona, to decide who gets care. Over a million Arizonans count on Medicare. Under Trump and RFK Jr.’s plan, AI companies will profit off denying care to seniors. This is wrong. Seniors deserve better.

Premiums will spike for as many as 22 million people who get their health insurance through the ACA next year. Why? Because of Trump and Republicans. What we need to do is work together to keep health care costs down. https://t.co/NgxqfwXl6a

Today we asked Republicans in the Senate to put Americans first and make sure healthcare costs don't get any higher. We need to fund the government and protect Americans' access to healthcare, but they’ve got to work with us to do that. https://t.co/xnAk99tIq9
